title: Amphibious Quadruped Journal
heading: A quadruped with leg-mounted floats walks into a basin, floats across and climbs out
eyebrow: Engineering journal · September 9, 2026 · MuJoCo 3.12 · Unitree Go2 model from MuJoCo Menagerie
lede: An unarmed Unitree Go2 model, used as a stand-in, carries four float capsules on its thighs. It walks down a smooth ramp into a calm basin, reaches its front legs forward so the floats point ahead, floats across on two idealised thrusters and climbs out on the far bank. The gait is a scripted crawl written for this one course; nothing is learned.
description: A MuJoCo Go2 stand-in with four thigh-mounted float capsules walks into a basin, floats 10.8 s unsupported on sampled-volume buoyancy and climbs out on a scripted crawl.

hero.caption: The complete crossing, replayed from the saved simulation in three synchronised views: following, side and overview. Walking plays at 8×; from 2 s before floating until 6 s after the exit begins it slows to 2×, and the current speed is labelled on screen. It opens on a 2 s still and holds the last frame for 3 s. Panels show buoyancy, weight, foot contacts and thrust from the run.

scope: Where it stands: one complete crossing of one known course, validated and recorded on September 9, 2026. Simulated: rigid bodies and contact in MuJoCo, plus our own buoyancy and drag on each float and on an assumed sealed hull. Scripted: the crawl gait, the float posture and the thrust feedback, all written for this scene. Idealised: the two water thrusters, which are applied forces rather than simulated propellers. Not claimed: that a real Go2 is amphibious, that the float sizes match any product, or that one crossing shows robustness.
footer: Source, documentation and recorded results: rozgo/mujoco-sandbox, docs/amphibious/. The robot is the Unitree Go2 model from MuJoCo Menagerie (revision 8161bba), copyright Unitree Robotics, used under its BSD-3-Clause licence with the original licence file and a SHA-256 manifest kept in the repository. The floats, basin, water model, controller and video are this project's own. Videos are rendered from the simulated trajectory and re-encoded for the web; nothing on this page is generated video.
